page: The Microsoft Azure L32as_v4 is a virtual machine instance from the Lasv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled as a local NVMe SSD with a capacity of 7679 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included.

In benchmark evaluations, the L32as_v4 demonstrates strong single-core and multi-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core and multi-core suites. Cryptographic capabilities are also strong, as evidenced by the Passmark CPU encryption test. For small language model inference, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 338.42 tokens per second and strong prompt processing speeds. Other workloads, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, database operations, and static web serving, perform within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L32as_v4 provides a high density of local NVMe storage and memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for data-intensive deployments without the premium cost of external storage arrays. The combination of 256.0 GB of RAM and 7.6 TB of fast local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance highly suitable for large-scale databases, data warehousing, and memory-intensive analytics. It is also well-suited for text processing, image processing, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
